institution: Regional Institute of Medical Sciences, Imphal
citation: Regional Institute of Medical Sciences, Imphal. RIMS Hospital Antibiotic Policy 2024 (3rd edition), section 3: RIMS Hospital Antibiogram 2022-23 (July 2022 to June 2023). Imphal: RIMS; 2024.
reporting: Percent susceptible with isolate numbers: Enterobacteriaceae for all specimens and by specimen (blood, urine, lower respiratory tract, superficial infection); P. aeruginosa and A. baumannii by specimen, A. baumannii by location; S. aureus (MSSA, MRSA) and CoNS from all specimens; E. faecalis and E. faecium by specimen and by location (OPD, ward, ICU).
method: Identification and susceptibility testing per the ICMR SOP (conventional biochemical or automated system); data entered in the ICMR AMR surveillance portal, validated by the regional administrator and analysed with the iAMRSN portal.

verification.note: Tables 2.1 to 2.5, the P. aeruginosa specimen table and Table 1.2 were parsed from the text layer (rotated column headers matched to values by position) and compared value by value with the rendered pages. The other tables are 72-dpi screenshots embedded in the PDF: each was read twice (the embedded image enlarged 3x, and the page rendered at scale 4 to 6 with different crops and nearest-neighbour zooms) and only values both readings agreed on were kept (one disagreement excluded). They were then checked against each other: the S. aureus column equals the MSSA and MRSA columns weighted by isolates, and the enterococcal Total columns equal the specimen tables weighted by isolates. Tables too blurred to read were left out (see excluded). Page numbers are PDF pages (book page = PDF page minus 14). Checked 2026-09-26.

notes: Section 3 'RIMS Hospital Antibiogram 2022-23' of the RIMS Hospital Antibiotic Policy 2024 (3rd edition; book pages 19 to 48, PDF pages 33 to 62), July 2022 to June 2023: 3,524 isolates studied (Table 1.1). The file was downloaded from the Wayback Machine copy (20240709) of the old rims.edu.in/secure URL and opens completely (164 pages). The report counts organisms in two ways: the organism table (Table 1.2) and the Enterobacteriaceae tables agree (E. coli 1,172, K. pneumoniae 545), but the non-fermenter, staphylococcal and enterococcal chapters use larger totals for the same period (A. baumannii 263 against 171, P. aeruginosa 314 against 234, S. aureus 554 against 470, E. faecalis 207 against 177, E. faecium 112 against 90); rows keep their own table's n and the organism counts are Table 1.2's, so these rows show count mismatches (source inconsistency). Some figures are not whole-number fractions of the printed n (for example A. baumannii ward 31.8% of 122), so for some agents fewer isolates were tested than the n shown. Colistin is printed 100 for every Enterobacteriaceae organism tested, including Serratia marcescens (intrinsically resistant). Specimen tables are for all locations; location tables are for all specimens (the enterococcal one except faeces). Gentamicin HL is high-level gentamicin. Where the report prints 0 for an agent in its trend tables it means not tested, so a 0 in rows with few isolates may mean not tested; values are recorded as printed.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 976 cells, all 83 row n and all 40 counts re-read against the pages (this includes the seeded sample of 244 cells over all 13 tables). Tables 2.1 to 2.5, Table 1.2 and the P. aeruginosa specimen table (p53): my own text-layer parse (780 cells) checked against the rendered pages. The 196 cells of the 72-dpi screenshot tables (p51, p52, p56, p58, p60, p61, p62): read by eye from the embedded images enlarged 4 to 12 times, written down before comparing. 0 corrected. Organism, specimen, setting, phenotype and page agree for all 83 rows.

Second reader: one first-read disagreement, resolved in favour of the file: p62 E. faecalis OPD penicillin is a single blurred glyph that I first read as 8; the file's 0 is the only value consistent with the Total (1.8) and ward (2.7) columns, so it stays 0.

Second reader: screenshot values cross-checked against the vector bar charts on the same pages (bar heights measured from the PDF drawing commands): the p52 A. baumannii location chart matches all 23 kept table values within 0.06 points, and the p61 non-urine and urine enterococcal charts match all 34 values within 0.1 points. CoNS and MRSA percentages are whole-number fractions of their n ('Staphylococcus spp.' CoNS as k/59 although n is printed 58), S. aureus equals MSSA and MRSA weighted by n, and the enterococcal location Total columns recombine from the urine and non-urine tables.

Second reader: all 59 cells the validator does not keep (14 cautions, 45 intrinsic) are in Tables 2.1 to 2.5 and are printed as recorded (text layer and page image agree). The 11 count mismatches are the source's two counting schemes (Table 1.2 against the chapter tables), as the notes say.

For the lead (not changed): the excluded p52 A. baumannii Total cefepime (image reads 7.5 or 7.6) is resolvable: its vector chart bar measures 7.44 while every other bar in that chart lies within 0.06 of its printed value, so the printed value is 7.5 (also my reading of the image). It could be added as 7.5.

For the lead (not changed): p61 urine E. faecalis ciprofloxacin reads 11.6 on the image (both readers), as does the p62 Total column (ciprofloxacin is tested only in urine), but its vector chart bar measures 11.52 and 19/165 = 11.5; at 72 dpi the last digit cannot be told apart from 5. Kept as 11.6.

Lead 2026-09-26: the p52 A. baumannii Total cefepime cell was added as 7.5 on the second reader's evidence (vector bar 7.44; the other bars of the chart within 0.06 of their printed values); p61 urine E. faecalis ciprofloxacin kept at 11.6 as printed in two places.
